title: Cabbage Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Cabbage Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Cabbage nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, boron and calcium in repolyo, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Cabbage nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your repolyo (cabbage) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, boron, calcium, potassium, phosphorus, magnesium, sulfur and molybdenum. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Small cabbage plant with pale leaves and yellow, reddish older leaves from nitrogen shortage
heroImage.credit: Rasbak (Wikimedia Commons user), CC BY SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus, magnesium and molybdenum move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But boron, calcium and sulfur stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which cabbage nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.
Cabbage nutrient deficiency signs, old leaves and young leaves
Shows first on the old leaves

rows: old, lower leaves, the whole plant

Muriate of potash 0 0 60, Sulfate of potash 0 0 50
Plants simply stay small and slow, sometimes with a pink or purple tint.

Outer leaves yellow between the veins and turn orange or red, while big veins stay green.
the whole plant, leaf edges and tips

blocks.text: Shows first on the young leaves

blocks.caption: Deficiencies that start on the young leaves of repolyo

Hollow, brown centre of the stem and light, loose heads.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a cabbage nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest cabbage nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in cabbage

blocks.alt: Small cabbage plant with pale leaves and yellow, reddish older leaves from nitrogen shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Rasbak (Wikimedia Commons user), CC BY SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

blocks.text: Older leaves turn yellow green first, then the yellowing spreads over the whole plant. Some leaves get a reddish or orange tint and dry patches. Leaves keep their shape but stay smaller, growth slows and old leaves may die. In severe cases the plant forms a tiny head or none. You see it most at this stage: from transplanting to head formation.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in repolyo
Sandy or light soils, heavy rain or irrigation that leaches nitrogen, low organic matter, raw straw or manure that ties up nitrogen. Very low or high soil pH.
How to tell it apart

Sulfur shortage starts on the young inner leaves. Phosphorus shortage slows growth but does not yellow the leaves. To be sure, old outer leaves yellow first. Confirm with a soil test and leaf tissue test.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency
Side dress urea or ammonium sulfate based on the soil test, in split doses before heading. For a quick green up, KAU suggests a urea spray at 10 grams per liter of water once every 15 days.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, add compost at land preparation and give nitrogen early, since the plant needs it before the head forms.
Boron deficiency in cabbage

Young leaves stay small, curl down and become deformed, with yellow mottling along the edges and between the veins and some dead patches. Heads are light and loose, plants look open and are stunted. The stem can turn hollow with a brown cavity, and heads taste bitter. You see it most at this stage: head formation.
Why boron deficiency happens in repolyo

Sandy soils where boron leaches, especially in the tropics, alkaline or overlimed soils, low organic matter, high nitrogen or calcium, and drought. Cabbage and other crucifers need more boron than most crops.
How to tell it apart

Hollow stem from very fast growth or too much nitrogen stays white and clean inside. Boron hollow stem is brown or discolored. To be sure, cut a few stems lengthwise to look for brown cavities. Confirm with a soil test and leaf tissue test for boron.
What to apply for boron deficiency

KAU suggests borax in the soil at about 10 kg per hectare (4 kg per acre) or a borax spray at 1 gram per liter of water. Delaware extension advises about 3 pounds of boron per acre before planting for cabbage, or, if none went in the soil, a spray of 1.0 to 1.5 pounds of Solubor per acre before heading. Do not mix borax with calcium or ammonium fertilizer.

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add boron to the basal fertilizer every cabbage crop on sandy soils.
Calcium deficiency in cabbage

blocks.alt: Cabbage head with brown, dried edges on the inner wrapper leaves (tip burn) from calcium shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: David B. Langston, University of Georgia, Bugwood.org, CC BY 3.0 US, via ipmimages.org

blocks.text: Dead brown lesions form on the tips and edges of young leaves and spread inward. Inside the head, the edges of inner leaves turn brown with a sharp border while the outer wrapper leaves look fine. So it shows only when the head is cut. It often gets worse near harvest and in storage, and soft rot can follow. Early, severe shortage stunts the plant so it may not head. You see it most at this stage: head filling, especially during hot dry periods of fast growth.
Why calcium deficiency happens in repolyo

Usually poor calcium movement into fast growing inner leaves rather than low soil calcium. Water stress (too dry or too wet), high ammonium, potassium or magnesium, acid sandy soils and large heads raise the risk.
How to tell it apart

Black rot (a bacterial disease) makes V shaped yellow lesions from the outer leaf edges with black veins. Thrips scars inside heads are small brown scratches, not dead leaf edges. To be sure, cut sample heads open to check inner leaves. Soil test for calcium and pH.
What to apply for calcium deficiency

Keep soil moisture steady. On acid soil, KAU suggests lime at about 250 kg per hectare when pH is 5.5 to 6, or about 840 kg per hectare in two doses when pH is 3.5 to 4.5. Gypsum on soil that is not acid. Correct boron at the same time.

Sold here with calcium: **Planters Products Lifelime** by Planters Products, Inc. (50.59 percent CaO), **Macrock Limestone** by Donumdei 1 Corp. (36 to 42 percent calcium), **Calcic Lime** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (35.52 percent calcium) and **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer for tomatoes](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes), and the page on [calcium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/calcium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid soil before planting, avoid heavy ammonium and potash, water evenly, and choose varieties less prone to tip burn.
Potassium deficiency in cabbage

blocks.alt: Cabbage with dry, scorched outer leaf edges from potassium shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Alandmanson, CC BY SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

blocks.text: Older leaves develop a light brown, dead band along the edges that spreads inward toward the middle. Leaf edges curl upward, and some leaves show yellow spots or stripes with dark green bases. Heads are smaller and loose, and in severe cases growth is badly reduced. You see it most at this stage: head formation and filling.
Why potassium deficiency happens in repolyo
Acid or sandy soils, heavy rain or irrigation, drought, low potassium reserves and soils rich in magnesium.
How to tell it apart
Magnesium shortage yellows between the veins with orange or red tints rather than a brown edge band. To be sure, soil test for potassium and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Apply muriate of potash based on the soil test, preferably in split doses. For an immediate remedy, KAU suggests a morning spray of sulfate of potash at 10 grams per liter of water with a sticker. Keep soil pH above 6 with lime or dolomite.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, include potash in the basal fertilizer and one side dressing.
Phosphorus deficiency in cabbage

The main sign is a strong slowdown in growth, often with no change in leaf color or shape. So it is easy to miss. Some plants show pink or purple tints on the leaves, yellowing leaf edges and weak roots. You see it most at this stage: seedling and early growth after transplanting.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in repolyo
Acid or calcareous soils, iron rich soils that hold phosphorus, low organic matter, cold or waterlogged soil and weak roots.
How to tell it apart
Root problems such as clubroot or nematodes also stunt plants. Pull a few plants and check the roots. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus and pH.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Apply phosphorus fertilizer near the roots based on the soil test. KAU lists single superphosphate for a quick correction and rock phosphate or bone meal for the long term, with best uptake near pH 6.2 to 7.0.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use a phosphorus starter at transplanting and add compost.
Magnesium deficiency in cabbage

Older leaves turn yellow green between the veins, starting at the edge and moving to the midrib, then orange or red. Small veins also yellow while large veins stay green, and the areas between veins curl upward. Severely affected plants may have normal sized leaves but fail to head. You see it most at this stage: head formation.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in repolyo
Sandy or acid soils, soils rich in potassium, heavy potash fertilizer, and cold wet periods.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen shortage yellows the whole leaf evenly. Potassium shortage gives a brown dead band on the edges. To be sure, soil test for magnesium and potassium, and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

KAU suggests magnesium sulfate in a band near the plants at about 80 kg per hectare (32 kg per acre). A foliar spray of magnesium sulfate gives faster relief. Do not apply magnesium and potassium fertilizer together.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use dolomite on acid soil over the long term.
Sulfur deficiency in cabbage

Growth is slow and development delayed. Yellowing appears first on the younger leaves, which can become purplish, curl upward and turn brittle. Head formation is held back, and plants are more open to fungal attack. You see it most at this stage: early growth and head formation.
Why sulfur deficiency happens in repolyo
Acid or sandy soils where sulfate leaches, low organic matter, waterlogged soils, and fertilizer programs with no sulfur. Crucifers need a lot of sulfur.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen shortage also slows growth but starts on the older outer leaves. To be sure, soil test for sulfate and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for sulfur deficiency
Use ammonium sulfate as part of the nitrogen, or other sulfur fertilizer. KAU suggests sulfur dust at about 25 kg per hectare (10 kg per acre) on sulfur deficient soil, and gypsum on alkaline soil.

Sold here with sulfur: **Farmfix Sulfur** by Philippine FarmFix, Inc. (99 percent sulfur), **VSI Sulfur Powder** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (99.5 percent sulfur), **Atlas Ammosul** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (21 0 0 with 24 percent sulfur) and **Philphos 21 0 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (21 0 0 (ammonium sulfate)). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [ammonium sulfate fertilizer](/blog/ammonium-sulfate-21-0-0), and the page on [sulfur deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/sulfur-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, give some sulfur every crop and add organic matter.
Molybdenum deficiency in cabbage

Leaves show a faint yellow green color all over. Young plants have small leaves that bend down with edges more toothed than usual. Older plants have long leaves that bend down. Plants grow loose and head formation is held back. In patches of a field, leaf edges may scorch. You see it most at this stage: seedling to early heading.
Why molybdenum deficiency happens in repolyo
Acid soils, especially pH 5.5 or lower, sandy soils and low organic matter.
How to tell it apart

Looks like nitrogen shortage, and patches in the field are typical. A test spray on a few plants tells them apart. To be sure, soil pH test and leaf tissue test. NSW DPI suggests spraying a few plants with sodium molybdate and watching for greener, normal growth.
What to apply for molybdenum deficiency

NSW DPI suggests about 50 grams of sodium molybdate in 100 liters of water sprayed on the leaves, or 150 ml of that mix at the base of each plant. For the next crop, mix about 1 kg sodium molybdate per hectare with the fertilizer, or water the seedbed with 40 grams in 50 liters per 10 square meters one to two weeks before transplanting.

Sold here with molybdenum: **Tierramino Molybdenum** by Unilox Far East Resources Inc. (16 percent molybdenum), **YaraVita Teprosyn Mo** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (15 percent P2O5 and 15.3 percent molybdenum), **Biozome** by Manchem Industries, Inc. (12 percent S, 12 percent Zn, 3 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 1 percent Fe, 1 percent Cu, 0.5 percent B, 0.05 percent Mo) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate General Purpose** by Sagrex Corporation (2 percent Fe, 0.5 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 3 percent S with Cu, Zn, B, Mo). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [molybdenum deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/molybdenum-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid soils to about pH 6.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any cabbage nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your repolyo needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Cabbage nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my repolyo leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: outer leaves turn yellow green with a red or orange tint and the head stays small or never forms. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at sulfur deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in cabbage?
items.a: Side dress urea or ammonium sulfate based on the soil test, in split doses before heading. For a quick green up, KAU suggests a urea spray at 10 grams per liter of water once every 15 days.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes boron deficiency in cabbage?
items.a: KAU suggests borax in the soil at about 10 kg per hectare (4 kg per acre) or a borax spray at 1 gram per liter of water. Delaware extension advises about 3 pounds of boron per acre before planting for cabbage, or, if none went in the soil, a spray of 1.0 to 1.5 pounds of Solubor per acre before heading.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes calcium deficiency in cabbage?
items.a: Keep soil moisture steady. On acid soil, KAU suggests lime at about 250 kg per hectare when pH is 5.5 to 6, or about 840 kg per hectare in two doses when pH is 3.5 to 4.5.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my repolyo lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the cabbage nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
